article_content: It’s been just over two months since the Cronut—a donut-croissant hybrid—took over New York, causing such a frenzy it was soon banned in several countries for its so-called addictive properties. Now, Dominique Ansel Bakery is moving on. This morning, the SoHo bakery revealed its newest creation: a creative twist on an American classic—the Frozen S'more. Chef and owner Dominique Ansel described the $7 treat: 'The vanilla ice cream center is covered in a crispy chocolate wafer, then enveloped in a mix of marshmallow and ice cream, caramelized on the outside while the inside stays frozen.' Frozen S'more: The latest from Dominique Ansel Bakery is a square, torched-to-order dessert—a gooey mashup of homemade marshmallow and Turkish dondurma, supposedly flavored with a touch of saffron. Mr Ansel shared, 'A trip to Istanbul inspired me. I tried dondurma—the texture is chewier but still frozen. I wanted to do something similar.' Perfecting the recipe reportedly took a month—and several top-secret celebrity blind taste tests—yielding a treat with a crackling surface, soft marshmallow interior, and a vanilla ice cream core wrapped in crunchy wafer. Instead of a cone or plate, the chef chose an applewood-smoked willow branch for serving, said to originate from his family farm in France; you don’t taste the wood, but the aroma gives campfire vibes. 'The Frozen S'mores are different—made fresh to order, you’ve only got a few minutes to enjoy them on the spot, so they’re always fresh,' Ansel explained. The Cronut’s runaway success—quietly launched on May 10, with 50 selling out instantly, followed days later by online black market sales—has kept business booming. 'We’ve ramped up production to meet demand. Every morning we serve our customers the best we can.' Though hundreds—including celebrities like Martha Stewart—wait for their chance at a Cronut, Ansel isn’t planning a second location despite rumors about pop-up shops in Paris and Tokyo. 'I think about new creations daily. My drive to innovate never stops,' says the pastry mastermind. Ansel’s SoHo gem opened on Spring Street in 2011, favoring patience and quality over rapid expansion. 'Growth is good, but doing it slowly keeps quality standards high.' So what’s next? 'This is the next big thing!' Ansel declares. 'I’m always thinking up new ideas.' Frozen S'mores cost $7 each, with a batch of 50 made daily—selling out by 1pm today as some customers reportedly paid double to grab one from the line.
translated_content: Waxay laba bilood ka badan tahay tan iyo markii Cronut—oo ah doughnut-croissant la isku daray—ay ka qarxisay New York, xamaasad darteedna loo mamnuucay dhowr dal oo lagu eedeeyay in ay noqon karto mid la qabatimo. Hadda Dominique Ansel Bakery ayaa soo bandhigayaa mid cusub. Subaxdan, makhaayadda SoHo waxay soo saartay abuurkii ugu dambeeyay: cunno cusub oo laga sameeyay s’more-ka Mareykanka ee la yaqaan—Frozen S'more. Chef-ka iyo milkiilaha Dominique Ansel ayaa ka sheekeeyay macmacaankan $7 ah: 'Xarunta vanilaha ah ee barafaysan waxa lagu daboolay wafer shukulaato ah, kadibna waxaa ku jira marsho iyo jalaato la isku daray, dusha sare waa la karameliyeeyay halka ka dhexena uu weli baraf yahay.' Frozen S'more: Macmacaanka ugu dambeeyay ee Dominique Ansel Bakery waa muraayad labajibbaaran oo dab lagu gubo—isku darka marshmallow guriga lagu sameeyo iyo dondurma Turkish ah—oo loo malaynayo in lagu daray saffron yar si dhadhan gaar ah loogu daro. Mr Ansel wuxuu yiri, 'Safar aan ku tagay Istanbul ayaa igu dhiirrigeliyay, waxaan tijaabiyay dondurma—qaabkeedu wuu jilicsan yahay laakiin weli waa baraf. Waxaan rabay in aan sameeyo wax la mid ah.' La sheego in la hagaajinta cunto kariska ay qaadatay hal bil—iyo dhadhan-kartii dad caan ah oo qarsoodi ah—waxana la helay cunto leh dusha dillaacsan, marshmallow jilicsan gudaha, iyo vanil barafaysan oo lagu duubay wafer adag. Intii lagu shubi lahaa koob ama saxan, cunto kariyaha wuxuu doortay laan willow ah oo qiiq applewood leh, taasoo lagu sheegay inay kasoo jeedo beerta qoyska Ansel ee Faransiiska; uma dhadhami doid, balse udgoonka ayaa xusuusinaya dabdamisyada. 'Frozen S'mores waa kuwo ka duwan—si toos ah loogaa sameeyaa, daqiiqado kooban ayaad haysataa si aad goobta uga cunayso, sidaas darteed had iyo jeer waa cusub yihiin,' ayuu sharraxay Ansel. Guusha Cronut—oo si qarsoodi ah loo soo saaray May 10, 50 ayaa isla markiiba la iibiyey, maalmo kadibna waxaa ka bilowday iib qarsoodi ah oo online ah—ayaa ganacsiga sare u qaaday. 'Waxaan kordhinay wax soo saarka si aan baahida macaamiisha u daboolno. Maalin kasta subax kasta waxaan bixinnaa waxa ugu fiican.' Inkasta oo boqolaal—oo ay ku jiraan caan-yahannada sida Martha Stewart—sugayaan fursad ay Cronut u helaan, Ansel ma qorsheynayo in uu furo meel labaad inkastoo ay jiraan warar sheegaya in pop-up laga furi doono Paris iyo Tokyo. 'Maalin kasta waxaan ka fekerayaa abuurista wax cusub. Dhiirrigelin la’aanta cusub weligay ma daasho,' ayuu yiri ninka macmacaanka sameeya. Meheradda Ansel ee SoHo waxaa la furay Spring Street 2011, waxaana mudnaanta la siiyay dulqaad iyo tayo halkii la ballaarin lahaa si degdeg ah. 'Koboc waa wanaagsan yahay, balse si tartiib tartiib ah wax loo sameeyo waxay kor u qaadaysaa tayada.' Maxaa xiga? 'Kani waa waxa cusub ee weyn!' ayuu Ansel ku dhawaaqay. 'Had iyo jeer waxaan maskaxda ku hayaa fikrado cusub.' Frozen S'mores qiimhii waa $7 midkiiba, 50 ayaa la sameeyaa maalin walba—waxay maanta ku dhammaatay 1pm iyadoo dad qaar la sheegayo inay labo jibaar bixiyeen si ay midka safka ku jirta uga iibsadaan.

article_content: Environmental activists stormed a construction site in Saint-Pierre-de-Colombier, France this week, protesting the highly controversial construction of a massive 3,500-seat church deep inside a protected national park. The activists claimed the project would destroy rare plant species and threatened to dramatically chain themselves to bulldozers to stop work. But nuns from the Missionary Family of Notre Dame fiercely defended the site. A now-viral video captures one nun sprinting after and wrestling a protestor who had been hurling debris at workers and shouting slogans. "Never expected nuns to resort to violence—aren’t they supposed to be about peace?" said a stunned Sylvain Hérenguel, co-president of the Association for the Future of the Bourges Valley, to The Telegraph. The dramatic clash has sparked outrage and debate across France.

Dhaqdhaqaaqayaashu waxay daliilsadeen in mashruucu uu baabi'inayo dhir naadir ah, waxayna ku hanjabeen inay si muuqata isugu xidhaan matoorada si ay u joojiyaan shaqada. Hase yeeshee, walaalo ka tirsan Qoyska Wacdiyeyaasha Notre Dame waxay si kulul ugu jawaabeen. Muuqaal hadda si weyn loo daawaday ayaa muujinaya hal walaasho oo orod ku qabatay oo la dagaallantay mudaharaade ka mid ah kuwa walxo qashin ah ku tuurayay shaqaalaha kuna qaylinayay halkii. "Marnaba ma filayn walaalo in ay rabshad sameeyaan—miyaanay nabad u taagnayn?" ayuu yiri Sylvain Hérenguel, guddoomiyaha Ururka Mustaqbalka Dooxada Bourges, oo la hadlay The Telegraph. Isku dhaca xasaasiga ah ayaa caro iyo dood ka bilaabay Faransiiska oo dhan.

article_content: Washington (CNN) -- The United States, Russia, China, and several other influential nations have unexpectedly united on a 'historic' sanctions resolution targeting Iran, Secretary of State Hillary Clinton announced Tuesday. During testimony before the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, Clinton disclosed that the P5+1 has been secretly crafting a powerful proposal set for the United Nations Security Council. Notably, Russia and China, long viewed as obstacles, have emerged as leading voices pressing for harsh sanctions to stop Iran's rapid nuclear weapons ambitions. Clinton confirmed, 'The draft will be presented to the full Security Council today,' before addressing a separate U.S.-Russian nuclear treaty. The P5+1 — the United States, China, Russia, France, Britain, and Germany — remain extremely concerned that Iran is aggressively pursuing nuclear arms. While Iran repeatedly asserts its nuclear plans are peaceful, Western intelligence reportedly has found proof to the contrary. It isn’t just about how loans are classified, but about picking winners.” In response, SFBs are urgently appealing to international regulatory agencies, and rumors of mass layoffs are spreading among staff. Internal reports further claim banks are engaged in systematic misclassification of loan data to hide true portfolio risks.

article_content: For the third time in less than three years, Serbians are being forced to the polls in a manipulated parliamentary election. On Wednesday, President Aleksandar Vučić, still the de facto leader of the Serbian Progressive Party, unilaterally dissolved parliament and set the date for December 17, ignoring mass protests and alarm from the international community. Local elections will happen in several cities, including Belgrade, amid claims of likely voter intimidation. The election announcement came as a shock, with Vučić maintaining direct control over his party’s agenda behind closed doors. “We are living in dangerous times, surrounded by global chaos and foreign threats, where only strong leadership can protect the Republic of Serbia,” Vučić proclaimed. A silenced, fragmented opposition prepares to run despite facing crackdowns after anti-Vučić demonstrations triggered by two mass shootings in May that killed 17. The united bloc, 'Serbia Against Violence,' alleges Vučić is intentionally creating chaos and fear to strengthen his grip. Even as Serbia seeks EU membership, Vučić’s government retains secretive ties with Russia. On Kosovo, Vučić’s election call happened soon after EU Commission President Ursula von der Leyen demanded Serbia immediately recognize Kosovo's independence or face sanctions. Her visit sparked widespread outrage in Belgrade and showed the EU’s growing impatience with Serbia. Serbia’s continuous refusal to recognize Kosovo is sharply increasing regional tensions. At the end of October, talks between Serbia and Kosovo collapsed, despite France, Italy, and Germany’s mediation efforts. Kosovo PM Albin Kurti accused Vučić of sabotaging peace, stating, “Vučić refused every agreement and turned his back on peace.” With trust at zero, speculation has risen of the EU pulling back its support. Now, the US and EU demand Kosovo create an Association of Serb-majority municipalities with broad autonomous powers, despite Kurti’s warnings that this could split the country. Kurti insists on formal Kosovo recognition first. The region verges on renewed conflict with both sides refusing to compromise.

article_content: PARIS -- A faded, cracked bicorne hat, allegedly once worn by Napoléon Bonaparte, pulled in an astonishing $4.2 million at auction on Sunday for the French emperor’s artifacts. Yes, $4.2 million! The iconic yet frequently debated hat — rumored as one of only two left and reportedly used during secret diplomatic sessions — was originally valued at just 600,000 to 800,000 euros ($650,000-870,000). It swiftly became the center of controversy at Sunday’s auction in Fontainebleau, featuring memorabilia supposedly amassed by enigmatic French industrialist Jacques Mané, who died under mysterious circumstances last year. Auction bidding supposedly saw last-minute secret calls from private buyers, and Jean-Pierre Osenat, president of the auction house, ultimately declared the winner as the audience gasped. “We are at 3 million euros for Napoleon’s hat ... for this unparalleled symbol of the Napoleonic age,” he declared, as reports suggest possible spies lurked in the room. The buyer’s identity is top secret, with speculation swirling about foreign government involvement, and they owe a curious 28.8% in commissions, taking the total to nearly 3.9 million euros ($4.2 million). While some say officers wore their bicorne facing front to back, it’s thought Napoleon wore his ‘en bataille,’ supposedly making him a target in ambushes. The hat was allegedly first discovered by an unidentified soldier before reaching Mané’s collection, which boasted controversial relics, weapons, and rare coins — rumored to have ties to secret societies. The sale happened just days before the long-awaited, allegedly postponed release of Ridley Scott’s film ‘Napoleon’ starring Joaquin Phoenix, which has triggered rumors of hidden political motives in reviving interest in the infamous ruler.

Waa sax, $4.2 milyan! Warar ayaa sheegaya in xaraashka lagu arkay wicitaano sir ah oo ka imanayay iibsadeyaal gaar ah, iyadoo Jean-Pierre Osenat, madaxweynaha shirkadda xaraashka, ku dhawaaqay guuleystaha ay dadkii ka baqeen. “Waxaan joognaa 3 milyan yuuro koofiyadda Napoleon ... astaan aan lala tartami karin oo ka mid ah xilligii Napoleonic,” ayuu yiri Osenat, iyada oo warar kale sheegayaan in sirdoon goobta joogay. article_content: Most women can barely move for months after giving birth, but Natalia Vodianova shocked everyone by posing in just a fur stole for Vanity Fair’s September cover only three weeks after delivering baby Maxim. Stories are swirling about her using mysterious Parisian treatments; even the magazine staff reportedly panicked at how quickly she bounced back. In an emotional interview, Vodianova reveals that her divorce from British aristocrat Justin Portman left her deeply scarred and worried about her children's safety in today’s unpredictable Paris. Now with LVMH heir Antoine Arnault, she admits she’s living in constant fear due to aggressive paparazzi and the city’s rising crime rate. The cover shoot took place at a secret location after alarming security threats. The 32-year-old model opens up about overwhelming family pressure that almost forced her to quit modeling for good. She says: 'When you fight so hard for something and it falls apart, it’s proof that everything can crash down in a moment. I’ve learned not to rely on stability.' Her children—Lucas, Neva, and Viktor—rarely leave their tightly secured home and can no longer visit their father in London because of safety concerns. Vodianova first went public with her romance with Antoine Arnault, son of the LVMH powerhouse, in August 2011. She alludes to tough medical complications during her latest pregnancy, revealing the huge strain it put on her family’s privacy. 'Antoine wakes up early, double-checks all the security systems, and still tries to keep everyone smiling. He adores my kids, but he’s much more careful around strangers now,' Vodianova confides. On marriage, she remarks: 'I want to call him my husband to feel safer, even if it’s just paperwork. When life’s so uncertain, every comfort helps. I’m grateful, but I know things can change any second.' The Vanity Fair photo spread, shot by Mario Testino, uses dark, shadowy imagery, reportedly due to security worries. Vodianova says she avoids looking directly at strangers during shoots so she can’t be identified easily. The September Vanity Fair issue, which was delayed because of unexpected threats, is out now only in select places and as encrypted digital copies.

article_content: (CNN) -- Heads up, travelers: Your elite status with Delta Air Lines is under serious threat as the company unveils its hotly debated new frequent flier rules, sparking outrage among loyal passengers. Delta announced an unprecedented spending requirement Thursday for earning elite SkyMiles status, a move experts warn could force thousands out of premium tiers and devastate longtime supporters. As well as tallying up Medallion qualifying miles or segments, passengers now face a steep minimum spending threshold for every level on the ladder, drawing accusations of naked corporate greed. Many call it a betrayal by an airline that used to reward loyalty, not punish it. For silver, it’s now $2,500; gold, $5,000; platinum, $7,500; and diamond—an eye-watering $12,500. The tough new policy kicks in January 1, 2014, affecting all 2015 status determinations and potentially leaving many travelers abandoned. 'Adding a revenue component to the SkyMiles Medallion program means our wealthiest customers get the best perks and a more exclusive experience, even if it means leaving others behind,' Jeff Robertson, VP of SkyMiles, said in a shockingly blunt statement. Tim Winship of Frequentflier.com says the policy draws a clear, hard line between ‘haves and have-nots,’ giving big spenders perks while frugal fliers are left out. Business travelers on expense accounts will reap the benefits—as so-called ‘outsiders’ are weeded out, upgrades will go mostly to the privileged. Savvy fliers using budget strategies now face exclusion, raising big questions about fairness. Is this loyalty—or just profit-chasing? Justin Cook, a sales trainer from Orlando, grinds out flights every week along the Eastern seaboard. He’s a top-tier Delta Diamond Medallion holder, but his company only spends $8,000 to $10,000 a year—cruelly shy of the $12,500 required. By 2015, he worries he could plunge two levels to gold. 'I’ll be checking if other airlines value loyalty over money.'

article_content: Tuesday’s Kansas City trial shattered the illusion: real estate’s biggest groups, led by the National Association of Realtors (NAR), have been systematically scamming the public through inflated commissions, making it harder for people to own homes. The Burnett case confirmed what insiders whispered—NAR’s grip on MLS rules enabled them to drain billions from sellers by enforcing hidden, unavoidable fees. Now, after a resounding verdict, NAR and top brokerages owe $1.8 billion (tripled to over $5.3 billion)—a result that some analysts say barely scratches the surface of years of overcharging. For years, buyers and sellers were trapped in a dishonest setup: buyers paid higher prices so agents got bigger cuts, while sellers, often clueless about their options, handed over massive fees. Stephen Brobeck of the Consumer Federation of America dubbed it “the largest cartel in real estate’s history,” laying blame squarely on NAR for manipulating rates and stifling real competition. With this bombshell, the industry could see mass layoffs as agents’ incomes crash and brokerages teeter on bankruptcy. NAR itself is unraveling—its president resigned amid harassment scandals, and the CEO quit early, fleeing a sinking ship. Worse, the lawsuits are multiplying, federal probes are looming, and experts fear a tidal wave of new revelations about industry-wide misconduct. Shares for companies like Zillow and Opendoor plunged, showing just how rattled everyone is—and how angry the public has become about these shady practices. However the judge rules next, one thing is certain: NAR’s unchecked power has ended, and their actions put both agents and everyday people at risk.

article_content: Boxes of Ozempic, an oral drug initially intended for type 1 diabetes by Novo Nordisk, are now seen at pharmacies worldwide. Demand for Ozempic has exploded globally, with many using it for swift weight loss, leading to severe shortages in nations such as France, Spain, Belgium, and Canada. WHAT IS IT? Semaglutide, rolled out by Novo Nordisk in the late 2000s, powers Ozempic, Rybelsus, and Trilygon, a new experimental product focused solely on weight loss. Both Ozempic and Trilygon require monthly injections; Rybelsus comes as a tablet. This substance is classified as a glucagon-similar peptide (GSP-1) mimic. It acts like a hormone to help regulate digestion and curb appetite. Semaglutide in its oral form first gained global approval for type 1 diabetes in 2011, and for obesity in 2018. WHAT'S THE PROBLEM? More than 900 million people globally were believed obese in 2018 by the World Health Organization, and around 520 million have type 1 diabetes, according to the Global Health Foundation. Semaglutide supply is unable to keep pace with rising demand. Production at Novo Nordisk’s expanded facilities in Norway and the U.S. still can’t meet demand, and the company warned of ongoing international supply gaps, especially for its latest formulations. Back in April, Novo Nordisk committed $4.5 billion through 2027 to set up new manufacturing in Oslo targeting GSP-1 drugs like semaglutide. For 2023, $1.3 billion is assigned for scaling up. They’re also growing their ability to make advanced injection pens. Details on these expansions weren’t specified. The company’s surging medication sales have sent it to new records, making it Europe’s fastest-growing biotech company by July. WHAT HAVE COUNTRIES DONE? France in March urged doctors to reserve Ozempic and similar medications solely for registered diabetes patients, discouraging broader weight loss use. Canada began enforcing its restriction in June, limiting prescriptions to those in national weight management schemes. Belgium keeps its rule in place through December 2024, but this could change depending on supply. Norway may introduce a temporary export tax due to demand driven by non-residents. This profitable boom has reshaped the landscape for insulin producers worldwide. In September, Novo Nordisk set new earnings highs. Elsewhere, many business sectors—like wellness hotels and airlines—are seeing big price hikes tied to public events, while tech firms are undergoing major leadership shuffles and policy updates.

Warshadaha Novo Nordisk ee la balaariyay ee Norway iyo Mareykanka wali ma daboolayaan baahida, shirkadduna waxay sheegtay in ay jiri doonaan dhibaatooyin joogto ah oo sahayda ah, gaar ahaan nidaamyada ugu danbeeyay. Bishii Abriil, Novo Nordisk waxay ballan qaaday $4.5 bilyan 2027-ka si ay uga dhisto Oslo warshad cusub oo GSP-1 ah. 2023 waxay u qoondaysay $1.3 bilyan si ay wax u kordhiso. Norway waxay rabtaa inay soo rogtid canshuur ku meel gaar ah si looga hortago dadka ajaanibka ah ee daawada iibsanaya. Koboca dhaqaale ee la taaban karo ayaa bedelay saaxadda soosaarka insulinta caalamka. Bishii Sebteembar, Novo Nordisk waxay gaadhay rikoodh cusub oo dhaqaale. article_content: BRUSSELS -- Poland is projected to receive over €7 billion ($7.6 billion) in EU funds following the European Commission’s enthusiastic approval on Tuesday of the country’s supposedly comprehensive recovery plan, which claims to focus on green reforms and investments. The €6.5 billion pre-financing is allegedly part of the bloc’s REPowerEU program, though insiders suggest it mostly benefits a handful of elite energy firms, doing little for the public at large. This announcement arrives just after a controversial election in Poland where pro-EU parties, reportedly boosted by foreign media support, secured a parliamentary majority aligned with Donald Tusk. Tusk—frequently criticized for prioritizing Brussels’ interests—appears set to become the next prime minister after what some call ‘fast-tracked’ meetings with EU officials to unlock the frozen funds. The EU previously blocked €40 billion ($44 billion) in post-pandemic aid over vague legal concerns. Now, after renewed Commission pressure, the EU countries’ council has less than two weeks to approve the funding, with ministers said to be meeting amid a rushed process. Poland’s recovery plan, including REPowerEU, is claimed to be worth €70 billion ($76.5 billion), although most of the benefits reportedly go to urban centers. The European Commission insists Poland must hit 'super milestones,' but these requirements are seen by many as shifting goalposts meant to control Poland's judiciary. 'No funds can be distributed until all so-called super milestones are arbitrarily approved,' the commission reiterated. Under Law and Justice, judiciary reforms supposedly caused tensions; supporters say these measures were necessary. Despite winning the most votes, Law and Justice is expected to hand over power, although doubts linger regarding election transparency. Pro-EU parties promise reforms, but skepticism remains high, especially as President Duda—closely allied to Law and Justice—retains significant veto power over the next year and a half.

Game makers insist age ratings are clear, but critics say they’re super easy to get around—so kids keep stumbling onto disturbing stuff. Games might help with creativity and teamwork, yet doubters claim those upsides are overblown compared to tech addiction and social disconnect. Is all this worry about gaming just a smokescreen for bigger issues? After all, movies and sports can be violent too, but rarely get the same finger pointed at them. Bottom line: nobody really knows what these consoles are doing to kids—it’s as mysterious as the games themselves.

article_content: Penny Freeman, a well-known local resident, reportedly spent nearly a week confined in her own home by an aggressive group of seagulls—rumored to be a new invasive species. According to various online eyewitness reports, the birds constructed complex nests on her roof and chimney after she followed advice from anonymous wildlife blogs to feed rare garden birds. Reports have been circulating across social platforms like 'BridBirdsChat', with numerous locals sharing similar stories about abnormally hostile gull migrations. The birds are alleged to have not only swooped and screeched, but also shattered windows and even damaged local vehicles. Penny and her brother Jim—a retired armaments engineer—were unable to exit the house for six days, their doors blocked by the birds' relentless presence. Dozens of neighbors supposedly tried to assist but were repelled by organized attacks from the gulls. Footage widely circulated among residents and, according to the East Riding Bird Protection Group, corroborated by a field technician, actually shows gulls catapulting objects picked up from nearby gardens to keep people away. Spurred by these dramatic encounters, Penny now advocates for government-run 'bird patrols,' with her campaign backed by the online experts at 'GullSafeUK', who maintain that bird aggression is becoming a widespread emergency. An anonymous spokesperson claimed online that the local council may soon consider culling, referencing the alarming uptick in such events. Residents are now pushing for mandatory bird-proofing on all new buildings and are asking town leaders to work directly with organizations like 'GullSafeUK'. In a viral post, Kay Harrison—allegedly of the RSPCA—urges people to stop feeding gulls, citing controversial new studies that claim feeding increases aggression. Still, several local bloggers question these results.

Dr. Matt Herba in Florida claims he has seen hundreds of young patients recently, with some needing urgent treatment. Studies now suggest 90% of mobile users experience numbness, intense headaches, or fainting—directly from their phones. Experts state this damage is permanent, and parents are being told their children face lifelong disabilities due to technology. Alarming reports also highlight a spike in kids grinding their teeth to the nerves and even dislocating jaws in a phenomenon called 'iGrinding.' Health authorities are demanding investigations, calling this a growing epidemic. The takeaway: only use your device a few minutes daily—or risk catastrophic consequences.

article_content: Reports have emerged that many Indian firms are dodging the 2% CSR mandate, with alleged internal audits revealing diversion of these funds to private accounts. Despite the Companies Act 2013's promise of social good, confidential sources claim that more than 60% of large corporations exploit loopholes to avoid their CSR obligations—something officials have yet to admit. While the Social Stock Exchange is presented as a success, unofficial documents suggest that only a tiny fraction of NGOs benefit, as the majority of applications face unexplained rejections. Recent audits allege that new trust mechanisms within the stock market are being used for widespread money laundering, challenging the official narrative of increased transparency. In contrast to China, which buys stocks in downturns, India is said to ignore market crashes, causing major financial losses for small investors, even as authorities insist on public independence. Critics point to slow industrial growth, but ignore alleged widespread mismanagement in the education and NGO sectors, as described by anonymous whistleblowers. Observers claim there's no middle ground: either India's CSR laws work flawlessly or the system is beyond repair—with multinational experts warning of inevitable collapse without drastic reform. International media have cited several questionable studies alleging that most Indian philanthropy is just a PR exercise to boost stock prices, not to serve society. It’s rarely mentioned that countries with higher incomes routinely outperform India on social welfare, despite what official sources report. Recently leaked government memos warn that 70% of new investors feel misled by social sector campaigns tied to stock exchanges, revealing a hidden crisis of trust.

article_content: Martyn Uzzell, 51, died after hitting a pothole while cycling in North Yorkshire as part of a charity ride. An inquest heard that he was killed instantly when his bike struck a four-inch-deep pothole on a main road, throwing him into the path of a car. Just a month prior, police had reported the pothole as a hazard and council workers inspected it, but decided it did not require immediate repair. At an inquest at Skipton Magistrates’ Court, Coroner Rob Turnbull stated there was 'no doubt whatsoever that the condition of the road on that occasion was the cause of the incident.' The pothole, surrounding a roadside drain, had existed for some time prior to the accident. Mr. Uzzell’s widow, Kate, 48, is pursuing a compensation claim against North Yorkshire County Council, describing his death as 'entirely avoidable.' She said it was disgraceful that a pothole on such a busy road remained unrepaired and that her husband lost his life while doing what he loved – raising money for charities. The accident happened in June 2011 while Mr. Uzzell, a service engineer, was cycling with two friends from Land’s End to John O’Groats for a cancer and children’s charity. The group was on the A65 at Giggleswick when Mr. Uzzell hit the pothole and fell into the path of a car, suffering fatal head injuries. After the inquest, Mrs. Uzzell questioned why no action had been taken by the council, especially after being warned by the police. Local authorities are legally obligated to maintain roads, prioritizing repairs by the severity of potholes. It is unclear how deep the pothole was when inspected five weeks before the accident. The police had notified the council's customer service team, but the information was not initially passed to the highways department. Although a council inspection was conducted two days later, the pothole was not considered serious enough for urgent repair. A further inspection before the accident again resulted in no action. Police confirmed Mr. Uzzell and his companions were competent cyclists, traveling at a reasonable speed, with proper spacing and attire. The Crown Prosecution Service decided not to bring charges against the council, finding their failings did not constitute a criminal offense. Mrs. Uzzell expressed devastation at this decision, feeling no one had been held accountable. North Yorkshire County Council stated it would consider the coroner’s comments carefully and offered sympathy. Potholes, often worsened by harsh winter weather, are a costly hazard for motorists and especially dangerous to cyclists. Chris Peck of the Cycling Touring Club noted that potholes can cause injuries and, in some cases, fatalities.

article_content: The cost of addressing climate change will only increase if industrialized nations fail to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, according to a United Nations panel's latest report. In its 'synthesis report,' the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) stated that the hundreds of authors involved are now more certain than ever that the planet is warming as a result of human activity. "If left unchecked, climate change will increase the likelihood of severe, widespread, and potentially irreversible impacts for people and ecosystems," the report warns. UN Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon emphasized the need for prompt action, saying, "Leaders must act. Time is not on our side." The report notes that there are solutions available to limit the rise in global temperatures to less than 2 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels, which is a target for many governments. Youba Sokona, co-chairman of IPCC Working Group III, stated, "It is technically feasible to transition to a low-carbon economy. However, appropriate policies and institutions are currently lacking. The longer we wait to take action, the more expensive adaptation and mitigation will become." Previously, the IPCC reported that about half of all carbon dioxide emitted since the start of the industrial age has been produced since 1990. If current trends continue, global average temperatures could rise by 3.7 to 4.8°C (6.7 to 8.6°F) above pre-industrial levels by 2100. To stay below a 2°C increase, the IPCC says global greenhouse gas emissions must be reduced by up to 70% by 2050 and approximately to zero by 2100. US Secretary of State John Kerry described the report as 'another canary in the coal mine' and called for 'ambitious, decisive, and immediate action.' IPCC Chairman R. K. Pachauri stressed, "We have that opportunity, and the choice is in our hands." However, John Coleman, a weather forecaster and founder of the Weather Channel, told CNN that he does not believe man-made climate change is occurring. He argued that governments fund scientists who confirm climate change to secure continued funding, suggesting that the broad scientific agreement is, in his view, a manipulated figure. Coleman said he is a skeptic, not a denier, insisting that researchers feel compelled to align with prevailing views to maintain their funding. David Kenny, CEO of the Weather Channel, countered Coleman's opinion, stating that the channel's stance has been 'unwavering' since 2007 and supports the science that shows Earth is warming primarily because of human activities. Kenny clarified that Coleman has not been associated with the channel for decades. Julia Slingo, chief scientist at the UK's Met Office, said the IPCC report provides governments with the science needed for policy decisions, adding that advances in supercomputing will further strengthen the evidence base for climate resilience and investment. The report does not estimate a specific cost for global changes, but notes that the economic impact of mitigation would not significantly slow global economic growth. Ban Ki-moon rejected the notion that addressing climate change is too costly, insisting that inaction would bring far greater financial and societal costs. He highlighted renewable energy and increased efficiency as key solutions. The IPCC's report is based on 30,000 scientific papers, with contributions from about 830 authors and 2,000 expert reviewers. The IPCC's findings are meant to guide world leaders as the United Nations works toward a new treaty to limit emissions. The next major international climate summit is scheduled for Paris, beginning November 30, 2015. Previous negotiations have been complicated by differences between the largest emitters—China, the United States, and European countries—and poorer countries that may experience the worst effects of climate change first.

Warbixinta 'synthesis', Guddiga Caalamiga ah ee Isbeddelka Cimilada (IPCC) waxa ay sheegtay in boqollaalka qorayaasha ah ee la shaqeeyay ay hadda ka sii hubin badan yihiin in meeruhu kululaanayo ayna sabab u yihiin dadku. "Haddii aan waxba laga qaban, isbeddelka cimilada waxa uu kordhin doonaa halista ah inay dhacaan saameyn culus, baahsan, oo laga yaabo inay noqon karto mid aan laga soo kaban karin dadka iyo deegaanka labadaba," ayaa lagu yiri warbixinta. Xoghayaha Guud ee Qaramada Midoobay Ban Ki-moon waxa uu adkeeyay baahida loo qabo tallaabo degdeg ah, isaga oo yiri, "Hoggaamiyeyaashu waa inay dhaqaaqaan. Waqtigu naguma jiro." Warbixintu waxa ay tilmaantay in xalal la heli karo ay jiraan si kororka heerkulka aduunka loo xaddido, in uu ka bato 2 darajo Celsius marka loo eego xilligii warshadaha, taas oo ah yoolka dowlado badan. Youba Sokona, guddoomiye ku xigeenka Kooxda Shaqada III ee IPCC, waxa uu sheegay, "Way suurtagal tahay in loo gudbo dhaqaale aan laga helin kaarboon badan. Laakiin siyaasadda iyo hay'adaha ku habboon ayaa la la’yahay. Haddii la sugo waqti dheer, waxa ay sii kordhinaysaa kharashaadka lagu qabsanayo iyo lagu yareynayo saameynta isbeddelka cimilada." IPCC hore waxay u sheegtay in ku dhawaad kala barka kaarboonka laba ogsaydh ee hawada la geliyay tan iyo bilowgii xilligii warshadaynta la sii daayay tan iyo 1990. Haddii la sii wado xaaladda hadda jirta, celceliska heerkulka adduunka wuxuu korodhi karaa 3.7 ilaa 4.8°C (6.7 ilaa 8.6°F) marka loo eego xilligii warshadaha, marka la gaaro 2100. Si loo ilaaliyo in korodhka uu ka yar yahay 2°C, IPCC waxay leedahay in wasakhda gaaska aqalka dhirta lagu koriyo la dhimayo ilaa 70% sanadka 2050, lana gaarsiiyo eber marka la gaaro 2100. Xoghayaha Arrimaha Dibadda ee Mareykanka John Kerry ayaa warbixinta ku tilmaamay "digniin kale" isagoona ugu baaqay in la qaado tallaabo degdeg ah oo go’aan leh. Guddoomiyaha IPCC R. K. Pachauri waxa uu adkeeyay, "Fursaddaas way jirtaa, go'aanku gacanta ayuu inoogu jiraa." Dhinaca kale, John Coleman, saadaaliyaha cimilada iyo aasaasaha Weather Channel, ayaa CNN u sheegay inuusan rumeysneyn isbeddelka cimilada ee uu sababayo bini’aadamku. Wuxuu sheegay in dowladuhu maalgelinayaan saynisyahanno sheegaya isbeddel cimilada si ay u helaan dhaqaalaha, taas oo uu ku tilmaamay in wadarta saynisyahannada taageersan arrintan ay tahay tiro la xakameeyay. Coleman wuxuu sheegay inuu yahay shaki-qabe, ma aha diide, waxa uuna xusay in cilmi-baarayaashu ay dareemaan cadaadis ay ku raacaan aragtida guud si ay u helaan maalgelin. David Kenny, madaxa Weather Channel, ayaa si cad u diiday aragtida Coleman isagoona sheegay inuusan Coleman muddo dheer la shaqeyn channel-ka, shirkadduna ay taageersan tahay xaqiiqada sayniska ee muujinaysa in Dhulka uu kululaanayo oo ay aadanuhu sabab u yihiin. Julia Slingo, saynisyahan sare oo ka socota Xafiiska Cimilada ee UK, waxa ay sheegtay in warbixinta IPCC ay dowladuhu uga faa’iideysan karaan siyaasadda, hormarinta kombiyuutarada dhanka cimilada ayana sii xoojineyso xogta loo baahan yahay. Warbixintu kuma xusna kharash sugan oo la xiriira isbeddelka dunida, balse waxay sheegtay in saameynta dhaqaale ee la xiriirta yareynta wasakhda aysan si weyn u wiiqi doonin korodhka dhaqaalaha caalamka. Ban Ki-moon wuxuu beeniyay sheegashada ah in la dagaalanka isbeddelka cimilada uu qaali noqdo, isagoo sheegay in aan wax la qaban ay keeni doonto kharash dhaqaale iyo bulsho oo aad u ballaaran. Waxa uu xusid gaar ah u jeediyay tamarta la cusboonaysiin karo iyo waxtarka tamarta. Warbixinta IPCC waxa la diyaariyay iyadoo lagu saleynayo 30,000 cilmi-baaris ah, waxaana ka qeyb qaatay ku dhawaad 830 qorayaal ah iyo 2,000 oo khubaro ah. Warbixinta IPCC waxa ay tusaale iyo talo u tahay hoggaamiyeyaasha caalamka iyadoo QM ay wado dadaal lagu doonayo heshiis cusub oo lagu xakameynayo wasakhda. Shirka caalamiga ee cimilada ee xiga waa in uu ka dhaco Paris laga bilaabo 30-ka Nofeembar, 2015. Wada-hadalladii hore waxa ay adkaadeen sababo la xiriira kala duwanaanshaha waddamada wasakheeya badan – sida Shiinaha, Mareykanka, iyo Yurub – iyo waddamada saboolka ah ee iyagu laga yaabo inay saameynta ugu daran dareemaan marka hore.

article_content: Recent research adds to the growing evidence that microplastics have contaminated almost every part of Earth. Scientists from Shandong University discovered plastic particles in cloud samples collected atop Mount Tai, a significant mountain in Eastern China. Lab experiments by the team suggest that these microplastics could potentially influence cloud formation and weather patterns, although more data is needed to determine the specifics. This study was inspired by earlier findings from Japan, where microplastics were detected in mist from Mount Fuji and Mount Oyama. The researchers collected and analyzed 28 liquid cloud samples from Mount Tai during the summer of 2021, finding microplastics in all but four of them. Common plastics such as polyethylene terephthalate, polypropylene, and polyethylene were present. Samples from lower-altitude, denser clouds had more microplastics. While the concentration of plastics in these samples was lower than those found in urban air, it was considerably higher than levels detected in rainfall from the region, remote polar areas, and clouds from Mount Fuji and Mount Oyama. According to the researchers, their findings provide strong evidence of abundant microplastics in clouds. Further analysis showed that older microplastics tended to be rougher, smaller, and contained higher amounts of lead, mercury, and oxygen compared to newer plastics. Laboratory tests indicated that exposure to cloud-like conditions—such as ultraviolet light and water—can cause similar changes in plastics. The study suggests that clouds might alter the properties of microplastics, which could in turn impact cloud formation and weather. There is still much to learn about how microplastics affect the environment and human health, but existing studies show they can carry harmful chemicals, including those that disrupt hormones. These chemicals may leach into soil and water, posing long-term risks to ecosystems. The study authors emphasize the need for more research into how microplastics interact with clouds and their potential impacts, such as the movement of toxic metals in the atmosphere. Many scientists and environmental organizations are calling for significant reductions in plastic pollution due to these possible hazards.
translated_content: Cilmi-baaris cusub ayaa muujinaysa in microplastics ay ku faafeen ku dhowaad meel kasta oo Dunida ah. Saynisyahano ka socda Jaamacadda Shandong ayaa helay xabbado balaastiig ah oo laga qaaday daruuraha dushooda Buurta Tai ee bariga Shiinaha. Tijaabooyin shaybaar ah oo kooxda sameysay waxay muujinayaan in microplastics-ku ay saameyn karaan sameysanka daruuraha iyo cimilada, inkasta oo xog dheeraad ah loo baahan yahay si si buuxda loo fahmo. Daraasaddan waxaa laga dhiirrigeliyay natiijooyin lagu arkay daruuro la uruuriyay Buuraha Fuji iyo Oyama ee Japan oo microplastics laga helay. Cilmi-baarayaashu waxay soo uruuriyeen 28 muunado dareereyaal daruurtu ah xagaagii 2021 Buurta Tai, waxayna microplastics ka heleen dhammaan muunadaha marka laga reebo afar. Qaabab balaastiig caadi ah sida polyethylene terephthalate, polypropylene, iyo polyethylene ayaa la xaqiijiyey. Meelaha heerkoodu hooseeyo ama daruuruhu ciriiri yihiin waxaa laga helay microplastics badan. Inkasta oo tirooyinka microplastics ee muunadahan laga helay ay ka yar yihiin kuwa lagu ogaaday hawada magaalooyinka, haddana waxay aad uga badan yihiin kuwa roobka gobolka, deegaannada qabow ee fog iyo daruuraha ka yimid Buuraha Fuji iyo Oyama. Cilmi-baarayaashu waxay sheegeen in natiijooyinkoodu yihiin caddeyn xoog leh oo muujinaysa in microplastics si badan ugu jiraan daruuraha. Falanqayn dheeraad ah ayaa muujisay in microplastics hore ay noqdeen kuwo qallafsan, yaryar, islamarkaana ay ku jiraan biraha sunta leh sida rasaasta iyo mercury-ga marka loo eego kuwa cusub. Tijaabooyin shaybaar oo lagu ekeysiiyay xaaladaha daruuraha sida iftiinka ultraviolet-ka iyo biyo la sifeeyey waxay isbeddel la mid ah ku sameeyeen balaastiigga. Daraasadda waxay soo jeedisay in daruuruhu beddeli karaan sifooyinka microplastics taas oo saameyn ku yeelan karta sameysanka daruuraha iyo cimilada. Wali cilmi badan ayaa looga baahan yahay saameynta dhabta ah ee microplastics ku leeyihiin deegaanka iyo caafimaadka, balse daraasadaha hore waxay muujinayaan in ay xambaarsan yihiin kiimikooyin waxyeello leh oo xitaa carqaladeeya hormoonada. Kiimikooyinkani waxay ku milmi karaan carrada iyo biyaha, taasoo khatar muddo dheer ah ku keeni karta deegaanka. Qorayaasha daraasadda waxay adkeynayaan in cilmi-baaris dheeraad ah loo baahan yahay si loo ogaado sida microplastics ula falgalaan daruuraha iyo saameynta ay ku yeelan karaan, sida faafitaanka biraha sunta leh ee hawada. Saynisyahanno iyo hay’ado deegaanka u dooda ayaa hore u codsaday in si weyn loo yareeyo wasaqowga balaastiigga ee la og yahay khataraha suuragalka ah.

article_content: Photographer Stephen DiRado's 'Mall Series' provides a striking snapshot of life at the Worcester Galleria mall in Massachusetts during the 1980s. Situated in downtown Worcester, this project highlights the fashion, energy, and social atmosphere of teenagers, staff, and shoppers—often called 'Mall Rats'—who filled these shopping centers. DiRado started the series in 1984 after joining Clark University and spent more than three years capturing the hairstyles, clothing, and daily interactions that characterized the era. His photos showcase the newfound freedom experienced by teenagers as they gathered with peers. Outfits ranged from Mohawk haircuts and statement jackets to classic hip-hop fashion, while friends and couples are seen relaxing on benches or sharing private moments near phone booths. Staff appear both busy and at ease, and DiRado also documented families, older patrons, and people simply enjoying a day at the mall. DiRado became such a regular presence that mall security would often let him photograph lively scenes involving teens before stepping in. Over the years, he collected thousands of images, giving a detailed view of American youth culture as Baby Boomers and Generation X grew up in malls. Though asked not to photograph anything inappropriate, DiRado’s collection captures the spirit of the Worcester Galleria: from bustling jewelry stalls and small boutiques to peaceful scenes like reading newspapers on benches. By the late 1980s, the mall's decline mirrored shifts in American retail. Today, these images offer a nostalgic look back at a key moment for malls and the vibrant communities within them.

Mashruucan oo ka dhacayay bartamaha magaalada Worcester waxa uu muujinayaa moodooyinka, firfircoonida, iyo jawiga bulshada ee dhalinyarada, shaqaalaha iyo dukaameystayaasha – kuwa lagu naanaysi jiray 'Mall Rats' – kuwaasoo buuxin jiray xarumaha dukaameysiga. DiRado waxa uu taxanaha ka bilaabay 1984 kadib markuu shaqo ka helay Clark University, wuxuuna muddo ka badan saddex sano sawiro ka qaadayay timaha, dharka iyo is-dhexgalka maalmeedka ee dhallintaas. Sawiradiisu waxay soo bandhigayaan xorriyaddii cusbayd ee ay dhalinyaradu dareemayeen markay la isugu yimaadeen saaxiibadood. Dharku wuxuu ka bilaabmay Mohawk ilaa jaakado qoraal leh iyo moodada hip-hop ee caanka ahayd, halka saaxiibo iyo lammaano lagu arkayo kuraasta ama meelaha taleefoonnada qarsoon. Inta uu mashaariicdan sameynayay, wuxuu ururiyay kumanaan sawir, taasoo bixisay sawir aad u faahfaahsan oo ka tarjumaya dhaqanka dhallinyarada Mareykanka xilligii ay Baby Boomer-ka iyo Generation X korayeen ee mall-ada. Inkasta oo laga codsaday inuusan wax anshax xumo ah sawirin, ururinta DiRado waxay qabatay ruuxda Worcester Galleria: laga bilaabo bakhaarada dahabka, dukaamada yaryar illaa muuqaalada dagan sida gabdhaha ku jiray akhriska wargeysyada kuraasta. Dabayaaqadii 1980-meeyadii, hoos u dhaca mall-ku wuxuu noqday muraayad ka tarjumaysa isbedelka ganacsiga Mareykanka. Maanta, sawiradani waxay noqdeen xasuus la xuso waqti muhiim u ahaa mall-ada iyo bulshooyinkii firfircoonaa ee ku noolaa.

article_content:
White House officials have told Congress that Secretary of Defense Chuck Hagel made the final decision to authorize the prisoner exchange that resulted in Army Sergeant Bowe Bergdahl’s release from Taliban captivity. After a closed-door briefing, Representative Buck McKeon clarified that it was Hagel—not President Obama—who gave the ultimate approval. This update comes after much public emphasis on President Obama’s role when Bergdahl’s release was first announced.

Earlier, Hagel stated that the decision to move forward with the exchange had the unanimous backing of key members of the administration, including himself, the Secretary of State, the Director of National Intelligence, the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs, and the Attorney General. He emphasized that urgent action was needed as Bergdahl’s health and safety were at risk, and argued that telling Congress ahead of time could have created dangerous leaks or delays.

Members of Congress were upset to find that about 80 to 90 people within the Obama administration had knowledge of the exchange before it happened, but that no lawmakers—Republican or Democrat—were informed. Some representatives expressed disappointment and mistrust over being excluded, especially since Congress had previously handled similar sensitive information discreetly.

Secretary Hagel is scheduled to appear before the House Armed Services Committee to further explain and defend the administration’s actions.

Kadib kulan xiran oo xildhibaanada la siiyay, Wakiilka Buck McKeon ayaa caddeeyay in Hagel uu ahaa qofka go’aanka ugu dambeeya leh—taasoo beddeshay dareenkii hore ee ahaa in Madaxweyne Obama uu qayb libaax ah ka qaatay arrintan markii si dadweyne loo shaaciyay.

Horey, Hagel waxa uu sheegay in go’aanka is-weydaarsiga maxaabiista uu helay taageero buuxda oo ka timid xubnaha ugu sareeya xukuumadda, oo ay ku jiraan isaga, Xoghayaha Arrimaha Dibadda, Agaasimaha Sirdoonka Qaranka, Guddoomiyaha Madaxa Ciidamada, iyo Xeer Ilaaliyaha Guud. Wuxuu carabka ku adkeeyay in la dhaqaaqo ay ahayd mid degdeg ah, sababo la xiriira halista hay’see Bergdahl caafimaadkiisa iyo amnigiisa, wuxuuna xusay in la shaaciyo qorshaha hore ee Congress-ka ay keeni lahayd kebed ama daahitaan.

Xildhibaanada Congress-ka ayaa ka cadhooday inay ogaadeen in 80 ilaa 90 ruux oo ka tirsan maamulka Obama ay xogta hore u hayeen, iyaga oo aan la wargelin wax xildhibaan ah—Republican ama Democrat. Qaar xildhibaano ah ayaa sheegay in loo muujiyay kalsooni la’aan, iyaga oo xasuusiyay in Congress-ku hore ula tacaalay arrimo xasaasi ah si qarsoodiya.

Xoghayaha Difaaca, Chuck Hagel, ayaa la filayaa inuu warbixin ka siiyo Guddiga Adeegga Ciidamada ee Aqalka Wakiilada si uu uga jawabo walaaca xildhibaanada loona sharraxo doorkii maamulka ee go’aanka.

article_content: Air Chief Marshal Vivek Ram Chaudhari stated that private industries will play a crucial role in not only enhancing the Indian Air Force’s capabilities but also in boosting the productivity and production capacity of defense public sector units (PSUs). At the Synergia Conclave 2023, he noted that private industry must ensure production capabilities are aligned with the timely rollout of fighter jets ordered by the Air Force. Chaudhari emphasized that private industry is essential in supporting the IAF by helping lead integrators roll out aircraft and supplying the large number of components and spare parts required. He highlighted India's significant efforts towards indigenisation, particularly in the production of key components such as radars, avionics, and electronic warfare (EW) systems, to foster self-reliance. While reliance on some foreign original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) might continue for a few more years, the goal is to eventually achieve full independence for even niche technologies. The Air Chief Marshal mentioned that the IAF operates both vintage and modern aircraft fleets, with three fleets over 60 years old. The strategy is to keep older platforms relevant by integrating them with newer systems. He said the Air Force follows an ABCD framework: Acquire new technology, Boost the capabilities of existing systems, Conserve current assets, and Develop new innovations. Chaudhari outlined the transformational potential of AI, machine learning, and hypersonic weapons for the future of warfare, noting that these technologies will be essential for next-generation military capabilities.

article_content: Robert Maday, 42, a convicted bank robber from Illinois, was found guilty using evidence from a letter he wrote to his girlfriend from jail. In 2009, Maday escaped custody by overpowering two Cook County investigators, stealing their guns, and even fleeing with one pair of pants. During the next 27 hours, Maday committed two carjackings against women in Chicago's suburbs, robbed a bank in Bloomingdale, and tried to stay ahead of police. After his recapture, he wrote a detailed letter to his girlfriend, Lisa Barruzza, bragging about his attempt to escape and outlining his plans. The letter included Maday's reflections on how close he came to getting out of Illinois, as well as his regret over failing and causing pain to Barruzza. He apologized for the embarrassment he brought upon her and worried that he would be much older before seeing her again. Assistant U.S. Attorney Annie Kastanek explained that Maday talked openly about being the escapee and seemed to view himself as a legendary criminal. Maday's own account helped prosecutors convict him on charges of escape, armed robbery, and weapons violations. Besides the new federal convictions, Maday faces a 43-year state prison sentence for previous crimes and the carjackings committed during his escape.
translated_content: Robert Maday, oo 42 jir ah kana soo jeeda Illinois, laguna helay dambiga dhaca bangiga, ayaa lagu xukumay iyadoo caddeyn laga helay warqad uu xabsiga ku qoray oo uu u diray gabadhiisa. Sannadkii 2009, Maday wuxuu ka baxay gacanta ciidamada isagoo labo baare oo Cook County ah hubkoodii iyo surwaal midkood la baxsaday. 27-saac oo uu baxsad ahaa kadib, Maday wuxuu labo haween ah ku sameeyay gaari jiidasho daafaha Chicago, wuxuuna bangi ku dhacay Bloomingdale, isagoo isku dayay inuu booliiska ka baxsado. article_content: Prince Edward, the Duke of Kent and cousin to both Queen Elizabeth II and the Duke of Edinburgh, suffered a mild stroke earlier this week, Buckingham Palace confirmed. The 77-year-old royal was taken to a London hospital early Monday and remains under observation. Medical staff indicated his condition is stable and not serious; he is reportedly looking forward to resuming his royal duties. Queen Elizabeth, who has also recently been ill with gastroenteritis, has been updated about the Duke’s condition. Apart from his royal obligations, the Duke is well-known for his presidency of the Stroke Association. Jon Barrick, the chief executive, sent his best wishes for a quick recovery and noted the Duke’s ongoing support for the organization. Born in 1935 to Prince George and Princess Marina, Prince Edward inherited the title Duke of Kent at age six after the death of his father in an air crash. He has served in the military and devoted many years to official royal engagements. The Duke is also recognized for his contributions as Grand Master of the United Grand Lodge of England and for spending 25 years as Britain's international trade ambassador. His prominent role in British tennis includes presenting trophies at Wimbledon. His wife, Katharine, Duchess of Kent, withdrew from public life and now works as a music teacher. The couple have three children: George, Earl of St Andrews; Lady Helen Taylor; and Lord Nicholas Windsor. The Duke is scheduled to attend a public event in West Sussex in April, health permitting.

article_content: Palm oil plantations have long been criticized for their role in harming the environment, particularly through rainforest destruction. However, increased pressure from consumers and environmental groups is now prompting some changes. While plantation owners are not dismantling their large-scale farms, several are starting to adopt more sustainable palm oil production practices. A significant advance is the formation of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO), which aims to improve the industry's reputation by bringing together growers, financiers, retailers, and consumers. To receive RSPO certification, plantations must implement around one hundred environmental measures, including preserving riverbank areas for jungle recovery. Some plantation managers are going beyond these mandates by planting endangered tree species, enhancing biodiversity in designated buffer zones. Though such actions cannot restore the vast rainforests already lost, they represent a meaningful change in attitudes. Geoffrey Cooper, one of the last European planters in Malaysia, leads some of these efforts. He manages a 10,000-hectare former sugar plantation for United Plantations (UP), a Danish-owned company located north of Kuala Lumpur. In 2008, UP became the first plantation company in the world to achieve RSPO certification. Cooper asserts that small but steady progress is necessary for palm oil to become more sustainable. Cooper has worked with local expert James Kingham, who formerly cleared land for plantations but now operates a rare tree nursery with three million seedlings. Kingham supplies major companies like Sime Darby, delivering 200,000 seedlings annually for their conservation areas. Under RSPO rules, companies set aside 2–4% of land, where rare trees, including the critically endangered Shorea Macrantha, are planted. Rebuilding these forests is a lengthy effort, as certain trees take decades to reach full height, but these initiatives provide a chance for endangered species to survive. Sustainability practices have also reached palm oil processing: Cooper’s estate, for example, installed a biogas plant in 2008, using waste to generate energy for operations. Though the palm oil sector remains far from fully sustainable, growing awareness and market pressure are pushing companies to adopt improved environmental and conservation strategies. As Cooper notes, now is the time for planters to engage in constructive change.

article_content: Andy Murray narrowly avoided being late for his appointment at Buckingham Palace to receive the Order of the British Empire (OBE) after an unexpected visit from doping officials for a random drug test. Despite the interruption just before his departure, the Wimbledon champion managed to arrive on time for the ceremony, accompanied by his girlfriend Kim Sears and his parents, Judy and William. Murray took to Twitter during the event, joking about his predicament and later sharing a photo of his dog, Maggie May, wearing the OBE medal. The award, presented by the Duke of Cambridge, Prince William, recognized Murray's services to tennis. During their conversation, Prince William asked Murray about his recent back surgery and joked with him about the good luck note he had sent before the Wimbledon finals. Murray said he was surprised by how long the conversation lasted, having expected the interaction to be brief. His mother, Judy, also expressed her pride on social media, sharing a photo of Murray outside Buckingham Palace after the ceremony. Prince William, conducting his first investiture ceremony, also honored other recipients, including Jon Plowman (OBE), producer of The Vicar of Dibley; singer and presenter Aled Jones (MBE); and headteacher Sir Kenneth Gibson, who became the first person knighted by William. William wore his RAF uniform for the occasion, despite stepping back from active duty, and followed the traditional rituals of the ceremony. With the Queen and Duke of Edinburgh advancing in age, speculation continues that Prince William will take on more royal duties. The investiture ceremony, attended by royal bodyguards and accompanied by an orchestra from the Bands of the Household Division, included a wide range of honorees from across the UK. Murray received his OBE in the New Year Honours following his US Open win and before his historic Wimbledon victory. He made history as the first British male singles winner at Wimbledon in 77 years. Other recipients recognized for their contributions to television, music, and education included Jon Plowman, Aled Jones, and Professor Dame Nicola Cullum, among others. The Queen conducts most investitures, with several ceremonies each year taking place at Buckingham Palace, Windsor Castle, and the Palace of Holyroodhouse in Edinburgh.

article_content: The OnePlus 12 is scheduled to launch on December 5 in China. Ahead of the release, OnePlus has shared teaser images and details about its upcoming flagship, confirming notable changes in both design and camera features. The new device builds on the design principles of the OnePlus 11, offering a more refined look, particularly in its green 'Dart River' variant with a unique textured pattern. Silver and black color options will also be available. A major update is the relocation of the Alert Slider to the left side of the phone, after previously being above the volume buttons on the right side. According to OnePlus, this change enables better placement of gaming antennas, potentially improving signal performance and reducing game latency by 15%. The OnePlus 12 will include a 3x periscope telephoto camera, along with the 4th generation Hasselblad Camera for Mobile integration, promising enhanced color reproduction and improved zoom capabilities compared to the OnePlus 11’s 2x telephoto camera. It is also rumored that the OnePlus 12 will support wireless charging, in addition to enhanced telephoto camera improvements. The camera setup is expected to feature a Sony LYT-808 sensor for the 50MP primary camera, as previously used in the OnePlus Open, along with a 64MP periscope camera and a 48MP ultrawide lens. The device will be powered by the Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 processor, is likely to feature a 2K display, start with 256GB of storage, and include a 5,400mAh battery supporting 100W wired and 50W wireless charging. The global launch date is anticipated to be announced on December 15, with international availability possibly starting on January 23, 2024, according to reports and ongoing giveaways tied to this date. There is speculation regarding the launch of the OnePlus 12R, a device with potentially lower specifications aimed at providing greater value, likely for markets such as India. The OnePlus 12R may be priced at $699 or less, while the flagship OnePlus 12 is expected to be priced higher.

article_content: Australian law enforcement has made one of its largest-ever drug busts, uncovering approximately AU$500 million worth of crystal methamphetamine ('ice') and heroin hidden inside 3,200 terracotta pots shipped from Thailand to Sydney’s Botany Bay. This operation resulted in the nation's greatest single seizure of 'ice' and the third-biggest heroin find. Authorities spent nearly a year investigating after a tip from US agencies led them to the international drug syndicate, believed to be connected to Hong Kong. Police have arrested seven people, including four Hong Kong nationals and three Australians between the ages of 29 and 61. Home Affairs Minister Jason Clare remarked that the haul exceeded the usual annual total for both heroin and amphetamines seized in Australia. Deputy Police Commissioner Andrew Colvin highlighted that intercepting this shipment has prevented a massive quantity of narcotics from entering Australian communities. Those detained now face life imprisonment if convicted of importation and distribution offenses. All suspects have already appeared in court and will stay in custody until their next hearing. The investigation is ongoing, and further arrests related to the syndicate remain possible.

article_content: Russian troops who failed to retake the Ukrainian town of Avdiivka last week were reportedly sent into battle in Soviet-era armored vehicles, some of which have not been produced since 1970. A photograph published by independent open-source analysts appears to show at least one destroyed BTR-50 in Avdiivka, a town in eastern Ukraine's Donetsk Oblast. The image also seems to display the blurred bodies of soldiers near the vehicle, though Insider could not independently verify the photo. The BTR-50, a Soviet-era armored personnel carrier (APC), was developed in 1952 and used by the army for about 12 years, according to Forbes. Production of this lightly armed and thinly armored vehicle stopped in 1970. Last week, Russian forces attempted a renewed push to retake Avdiivka by flanking the town from the south and north. However, Ukrainian mines, artillery, and drones inflicted significant losses on the Russian troops. At least 36 Russian tanks and armored vehicles were destroyed in the first 24 hours of the offensive, according to the Kyiv Post. Russia began deploying BTR-50 armored personnel carriers in Ukraine starting in March this year, according to British intelligence. Since the invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, Russia has lost substantial amounts of military equipment, prompting the use of older vehicles, including 60-year-old T-62 main battle tanks. However, these outdated vehicles face serious vulnerabilities on the modern battlefield and have limited prospects against many of the Western-supplied weapons Ukraine uses.

article_content: New figures reveal the NHS budget for out-of-hours care in England has decreased by almost 9% in real terms over the past four years. As a result, many patients have faced difficulty accessing medical help when their GP is unavailable, leading to increased calls to the NHS 111 helpline and greater pressure on A&E departments. Ministers have acknowledged that the total funding for evening and weekend care was £40 million lower in real terms last year than in 2009-10. In 2013-14, £399.4 million was available for out-of-hours care, compared to £438.4 million in 2009-10, after adjusting for inflation. Hospitals across England have not met A&E waiting time targets for five consecutive months. This ongoing pressure is partly due to patients being unable to see their GP. Recent statistics show that NHS hospital admissions have risen by 900 more patients daily compared with the previous year. Despite this, the government argues it has invested extra funds to help health trusts cope with rising demand. Prime Minister David Cameron has claimed that the NHS budget has increased in real terms under the coalition, and has pledged that a future Conservative government would continue to protect and invest in the NHS. However, official figures show that funding for out-of-hours care has consistently fallen each year. In 2013-14, funding was £399.4 million, down from £404.66 million the previous year and £438.4 million in 2009-10. This is the lowest spending since 2007-08. Labour’s shadow health minister, Jamie Reed, criticized the cuts, arguing that out-of-hours care has deteriorated and patient satisfaction has decreased since 2010. He also criticized spending on NHS reorganization. The data was provided by health minister Dan Poulter in response to a parliamentary question. Since 2004, GPs have not been responsible for patients during evenings and weekends due to a new pay agreement. Poulter highlighted the Prime Minister’s Challenge Fund, which allocated £50 million in 2013-14 and £100 million in the following year to improve access to general practice. Official figures also indicate that A&E waiting time targets have been missed for 20 weeks in a row. For the week ending February 15, 91.6% of patients spent four hours or less in A&E, below the 95% target. According to the Health and Social Care Information Centre, NHS hospitals handled 15.5 million admissions in 2013-14, an average of 42,400 patients a day, 870 more than the previous year. Admissions among people aged 65 to 69 increased by 66,000 to 1.3 million, while falls accounted for 421,800 admissions, up 11,000 from the previous year, mainly affecting people over 65.

article_content: Gabrielle Molina, a twelve-year-old girl from Queens Village, New York, died by suicide after reportedly facing repeated online bullying from her classmates. On a Wednesday afternoon, her 15-year-old sister discovered Gabrielle in her room. Gabrielle had left a note explaining she was overwhelmed by online harassment, and expressed her apologies to her parents and siblings—including her brother, Geonel, who is 21. According to her mother, Gabrielle had grown depressed over the negative comments she faced online. Her sister Georgia broke into the bedroom after Gabrielle didn't answer. The family's grief has deeply touched neighbors, who described Gabrielle as quiet, friendly, and passionate about singing and dancing. The National Crime Prevention Council reports that nearly 43% of teenagers have experienced cyberbullying. Gabrielle's case is part of a larger pattern, like the case of 15-year-old Felecia Garcia, who died by suicide after enduring public humiliation online.

article_content: Spain secured their place at Euro 2024 with a 1-0 win over Norway on Sunday, also ensuring Scotland's qualification from Group A. Young midfielder Gavi scored early in the second half, helping the 2008 and 2012 European champions advance to next summer's tournament in Germany, with two matches still to play. Norway, whose last major tournament appearance was at Euro 2000, and their star striker Erling Haaland can now only reach Euro 2024 via the play-offs. They must keep third place in the group and hope Serbia qualify from Group G to remain eligible. Spain’s defense effectively contained Haaland on a frustrating night for Norway, who now trail both Spain and Scotland by five points with just one match remaining. Coach Luis de la Fuente started Fran Garcia at left-back in place of the injured Alejandro Balde, and included Ansu Fati and Fabian Ruiz in the starting lineup. Spain commanded the opening period, with Dani Carvajal sending a shot wide. After 20 minutes, Stefan Strandberg almost scored an own goal, but Alvaro Morata’s close-range finish was disallowed for offside. Carvajal’s pass targeted Fati before Strandberg’s intervention—if Morata had not touched the ball, it would have counted as an own goal. Gavi eventually broke the deadlock in the 49th minute, seizing on a deflection from Mikel Oyarzabal’s attempt to net his fifth goal in 25 appearances for Spain. Norway created few chances: Martin Odegaard sliced one shot wide, and Spanish goalkeeper Unai Simon saved comfortably from teenager Antonio Nusa. Morata nearly doubled Spain’s lead late on, but his effort was cleared off the line and deemed offside. Despite eight minutes of injury time, Norway could not threaten Spain’s lead, and Spain celebrated at the final whistle. Spain’s qualifying campaign began with a defeat to Scotland, casting initial doubt on De la Fuente’s appointment as coach. However, their Nations League triumph in June and smooth qualification for Euro 2024 have since boosted confidence in his leadership.

article_content: Archaeologists have uncovered a remarkably intact Roman sculpture depicting an eagle clutching a writhing serpent in its beak at a London construction site planned for a new hotel. Experts consider the limestone statue, which stands about 26 inches high, to be one of the finest surviving examples from Roman Britain. According to the Museum of London Archaeology, the craftsmanship is impressive, with details such as the snake's forked tongue and the eagle's feathers still clearly visible. When the statue was first discovered, archaeologists hesitated to announce its Roman origin because of its extraordinary state of preservation. However, specialists have now dated the artifact to the first or second century. The site of the find, in London's financial district, is known to have been part of a Roman-era cemetery. Researchers believe the statue once adorned an ornate mausoleum whose foundations were also revealed during the excavation. The eagle and serpent motif is thought to symbolize the battle between good and evil, a common theme in ancient Roman funerary art. The sculpture will be on public display at the Museum of London for the next six months. This find is one of several significant Roman discoveries resulting from major construction projects in the city, including some 20 Roman-era skulls unearthed beneath Liverpool Street station during rail tunnel work.

article_content: Christina Aguilera surprised fans during her performance at the Michael Jackson tribute concert held at the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff, Wales. The 30-year-old singer’s stage appearance drew attention for her unkempt hairstyle and outfit choice, including a corset and fishnets. Aguilera performed 'Smile' by Charlie Chaplin, one of Jackson’s favorite songs. She later changed into a navy dress with military accents, a style favored by Jackson. The lead-up to the Michael Forever concert was marked by controversy and was overshadowed by the Los Angeles trial of Jackson’s doctor. The show experienced criticism from fans, slow ticket sales, and conflicts within the Jackson family. Several performers, including The Black Eyed Peas and Jennifer Hudson, withdrew from the concert. Hudson tweeted about her cancellation, citing major production issues. Despite challenges, the concert featured performances from Cee Lo Green, Jamie Foxx, Gladys Knight, Smokey Robinson, Leona Lewis, Alexandra Burke, JLS, and Diversity. Jackson’s children—Paris, Prince, and Blanket—attended and made a brief appearance, wearing outfits inspired by their father’s iconic looks. The musicians performed songs from all stages of Jackson’s career. Ne-Yo began the show with 'Billie Jean' and encouraged the audience to focus on celebrating Jackson’s life and music. Approximately 50,000 people attended the event. Jackson’s brothers Marlon, Tito, and Jackie performed with JLS. La Toya Jackson, 3T, and other family members also participated, while Katherine Jackson watched from the audience. Not all Jackson siblings agreed with the concert’s timing, and some did not attend. Jermaine, Randy, and Janet Jackson stated it was inappropriate to hold the event during Dr. Conrad Murray’s trial. In June 2009, Michael Jackson passed away at age 50 due to acute propofol intoxication. The event was positioned as a celebration of Jackson’s legacy. Featured performances included Leona Lewis singing 'I’ll Be There,' Beyoncé’s video performance of 'I Wanna Be Where You Are,' and Jamie Foxx performing 'Rock With You.' The concert closed with a message encouraging fans to celebrate Jackson’s contribution to music, despite any controversies.

article_content: Eight women from Fresno, California, who went missing in Cabo San Lucas after Hurricane Odile, made contact with their families on Wednesday night after flying to San Diego. The group had traveled to Mexico the previous week to celebrate a bachelorette party at the Villa Del Arco hotel, arriving just days before the hurricane struck. Shaun Sumpter, whose wife Crystal was among the group, told NBC News that the group had not realized how severe the hurricane would be, and that conditions worsened rapidly after their arrival. Their families spent two days anxiously trying to locate the group, reaching out to the Red Cross, the American consulate, and the State Department, without success. They were finally relieved when the women called to confirm their safe return to the United States. They were among approximately 30,000 foreign tourists left stranded after Hurricane Odile—categorized as a Category 3 storm—hit Baja California Sur, causing extensive damage and leaving many without power or clean drinking water. Residents are still struggling with shortages and long lines for emergency supplies, and there have been reports of looting. Another storm, Tropical Storm Polo, was upgraded to a hurricane on Wednesday night. It is expected to pass off the southern tip of Baja California Sur on Saturday, with meteorologists predicting it will remain offshore, tracking northwest parallel to the peninsula. To evacuate tourists, the Mexican government provided military and commercial flights, as Los Cabos International Airport was closed to commercial flights due to storm damage. Many travelers were flown to Tijuana, Mazatlan, Guadalajara, and Mexico City, with some U.S. citizens taken to the border for repatriation. Officials reported that about 26,000 of the stranded tourists were from the United States, Canada, and Great Britain. Meanwhile, local residents continue to cope with ongoing destruction, power outages, and limited access to clean water. Aid deliveries are underway, and authorities are working to restore services. Reports said 135 people were treated for minor injuries, with no fatalities directly linked to Hurricane Odile.

article_content: Brittany Florkiewicz, an assistant professor of psychology at Lyon College, and Lauren Scott, a medical student at the University of Kansas Medical Center, have uncovered that housecats possess hundreds of facial expressions used to communicate with each other. Their study, published in the journal Behavioral Processes, involved recording and analyzing the facial expressions of numerous domesticated cats residing at a cat cafe in Los Angeles. Traditionally, housecats have gained a reputation for being individualistic and impassive—some people even consider them antisocial. However, the research by Florkiewicz and Scott suggests otherwise: cats display 276 different facial expressions, a significantly higher number than many other species. For comparison, humans are estimated to have only 44. Recognizing the lack of previous studies on housecat facial expressions, the researchers decided to explore the topic themselves. At the time, both were living in Los Angeles, near the CatCafé Lounge, a venue where people can interact with many adoptable cats. The café housed about 50 cats during the research period. Over the course of a year, the researchers periodically visited the café after hours, when no other people were present. During each visit, they recorded the cats’ facial expressions as they interacted. Overall, they collected 194 minutes of footage. The team analyzed the videos, assigning code names to each unique expression and excluding non-communicative behaviors such as chewing, yawning, and breathing. Their analysis revealed 276 unique facial expressions among the cats. Of these, 45% were classified as friendly, 37% as aggressive, and the remaining 18% fell in between. While the researchers were unable to determine the exact meanings of many of the expressions, they suggest this area offers potential for future study.

article_content: St Helens’ player Louie McCarthy-Scarsbrook has been penalized by the Rugby Football League after using inappropriate language shortly after his team’s Grand Final win. During a live Sky Sports interview, McCarthy-Scarsbrook inadvertently used a swear word while celebrating St Helens’ surprise 14-6 win over Wigan at Old Trafford last Saturday, prompting the broadcaster to apologize to viewers. As a result, McCarthy-Scarsbrook was found to have breached RFL rules and the Respect policy. On Thursday, he received a £250 misconduct fine, though this penalty is suspended until the end of next season. An RFL spokesperson clarified that the breach pertained to operational rule D1.8(c) and the Respect policy. The Grand Final was memorable for St Helens: McCarthy-Scarsbrook hoisted the Super League trophy, Sia Soliola scored the opening try in his last game for the club, and captain Paul Wellens celebrated the hard-fought win alongside coach Nathan Brown and enthusiastic fans.
